headline: Alphabet and Microsoft earnings land tonight US time — Google up 1.3% last night on strong expectations, while Aussie inflation jumps to 4.3% raising real RBA rate-hike pressure for next week.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a strong session today, up 3.8% to $2.99. There's no single major catalyst in today's news, but lithium stocks have been volatile on any signs of price stabilisation. The stock is still deeply underwater overall (down ~56% from your cost base), so today's bounce is welcome but the recovery thesis remains a long, patient one.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI gained 1.3% today, riding broader enthusiasm around AI stocks ahead of Alphabet and Microsoft earnings tonight. Positive sentiment around NVIDIA's expanded collaboration with Meta on AI models also helped lift the sector.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google jumped 1.3% last night as Wall Street built anticipation ahead of tonight's Q3 earnings report. Analysts are expecting around 25% revenue growth, driven by AI-boosted Search and Cloud. Bloomberg also noted investor focus on whether AI spending is starting to convert to cash flow — a key test for the whole sector.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up 0.6% today, likely helped by a slightly stronger Aussie dollar (up 0.3% to US$0.704) which often coincides with improving sentiment toward emerging markets.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS gained 0.35% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's mild S&P 500 gains of 0.16%. Broad US market sentiment remains positive heading into a big earnings week.

movers.name: DHHF ETF
movers.note: DHHF ticked up 0.34% today — a quiet, steady session for this diversified all-in-one fund. Nothing specific to call out; it's just doing what it's designed to do.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up 0.17% today. A gentle positive session with no specific news catalyst — the fund's global diversification continues to smooth out day-to-day noise.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dipped a modest 0.25% last night ahead of its own Q1 earnings report due tonight US time. Wall Street is watching Azure cloud growth as the key number — any sign AI is driving real revenue will be the swing factor. The dip is tiny and likely reflects pre-earnings caution rather than any negative news.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 0.4% last night. There's ongoing chatter about whether GTA 6 might slip to 2027, which keeps a lid on the stock. On the positive side, Bank of America reiterated a buy rating last night, calling TTWO a buy ahead of a GTA 6-fuelled earnings boom. A Rockstar Games workers' union vote is also in the news, adding a small wild card.

watch_today.title: GOOG & MSFT Earnings Tonight — Big Night for Your Portfolio
watch_today.detail: Both Alphabet (GOOG) and Microsoft (MSFT) report Q3/Q1 earnings tonight US time (after their market opens ~11:30 PM AEST). Wall Street expects Alphabet to show ~25% revenue growth driven by AI Search and Cloud. For Microsoft, Azure growth is the key number. These are two of your holdings and the results will set the tone for the entire tech sector. No action needed before results — just be aware your portfolio could move noticeably by tomorrow morning.

watch_today.title: MSFT Earnings — Hold Heading Into Tonight
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is down a tiny 0.25% in last night's pre-earnings session — nothing alarming. The long-term AI infrastructure story is intact. If Azure growth comes in strong tonight, expect a pop. If it misses, any dip would likely be a long-term buying opportunity rather than a reason to panic. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: RBA Rate Decision — Now Looking Like a Hike Next Week
watch_today.detail: Australia's inflation jumped to 4.3% in the latest reading, well above expectations. CommBank economists are now forecasting a rate hike at next Tuesday's RBA meeting. A rate rise would mean higher mortgage costs for many Aussies and could weigh on ASX-listed property and consumer stocks. Keep an eye on how your broader ETFs (VDHG, DHHF) react if the hike is confirmed.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Good Day, But Don't Get Too Excited
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals bounced 3.8% today to $2.99, which is a nice session. But you're still down around 56% on this position from your cost base. The lithium market remains under pressure globally. The long-term electric vehicle thesis is intact, but recovery will take time. Hold and be patient — don't let one green day change your long-term view.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 Delay Rumours vs BofA Buy Rating
watch_today.detail: Take-Two slipped slightly last night, with lingering speculation about a potential GTA 6 delay to 2027 keeping some investors cautious. However, Bank of America reiterated a buy call, expecting a GTA 6-fuelled earnings surge. You're currently down ~7% on this position. The long-term case rests entirely on GTA 6 being a blockbuster — hold for now, but watch for any official delay announcement as that would be a meaningful setback.

watch_today.title: Oil Spiking on Iran-US War Risk — Watch Your Energy Exposure
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped 1.9% last night to US$101.83 a barrel after reports that the US warned Gulf states of a possible short, intense military conflict with Iran after the US midterms. Gulf states are reportedly scrambling to broker a peace deal. Higher oil prices feed into Australian inflation and can weigh on the broader economy — worth keeping an eye on this week.

world.summary: The dominant global story today is rising US-Iran war risk ahead of American midterm elections, with Gulf states scrambling to broker a ceasefire deal. US midterm politics is also front and centre, with Trump making unsubstantiated voter fraud claims. Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro has left Brazil for the US after a presidential election defeat, and global inflation is expected to stay elevated into next year.

stories.title: US Warns of Possible Iran War Flare-Up After Midterms — Gulf States Rush to Broker Peace
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has privately warned Gulf Arab states that there could be a short but intense renewal of the US-Iran war in the period just after the November midterm elections. Saudi Arabia reportedly offered Yemen's Houthis $1 billion in an Iran-mediated ceasefire proposal, and Gulf states are working on a multipart peace deal to avert a wider conflict. Iran has rejected a Qatar-brokered proposal as 'unacceptable'. The Houthis today also urged the immediate evacuation of Aden airport in Yemen, signalling active hostilities. This matters for everyday Australians because any escalation near the Strait of Hormuz — where a huge chunk of the world's oil passes — could send fuel prices sharply higher. Oil was already up nearly 2% last night to over US$101 a barrel.

stories.title: Trump Claims 'Rampant' Voter Fraud as Midterms Approach — Evidence Says Otherwise
stories.why_it_matters: With US midterm elections just days away, former President Donald Trump is publicly claiming voter fraud is 'rampant' in California and other states. The BBC reports that election officials and independent investigations consistently find voter fraud to be extremely rare in the US. Democrats, meanwhile, are preparing potential congressional investigations if they win back the House or Senate. The outcome of the midterms matters for global markets — a split Congress would limit Trump's ability to push through major economic or tax policy changes, which could affect everything from US fiscal spending to tariff policy.

stories.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Leaves Brazil for the US After Election Defeat
stories.why_it_matters: Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, has left Brazil for the United States following the Bolsonaro family's defeat at the polls. Brazil is a major emerging market and a key supplier of agricultural commodities and iron ore — political instability there can have ripple effects on global commodity prices and emerging market sentiment, which touches your VGE.AX holding.

stories.title: Global Inflation Expected to Stay Elevated Into 2027, Reuters Poll Finds
stories.why_it_matters: A Reuters poll of global economists found that high inflation is expected to persist across most of the world into at least 2027, with central banks remaining under pressure to keep interest rates elevated. This is directly relevant to Australian investors — higher rates for longer mean tougher conditions for growth stocks, more expensive mortgages, and continued pressure on household budgets. It also reinforces why today's Australian CPI print of 4.3% is so significant.

stories.title: China, Germany and the EU: Geopolitical Fractures in Global Supply Chains
stories.why_it_matters: Analysis published today highlights deepening tensions in the global economic relationship between China, Germany, and the EU over trade and supply chains. Germany relies heavily on Chinese manufacturing inputs while the EU is pushing to 'de-risk' from China — a tension that could reshape global trade flows. For Australian investors, China remains our biggest export customer, so any significant shift in how China trades with Europe can flow through to demand for Australian iron ore, coal, and lithium.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 was essentially flat today, dipping just 0.03% to 8,847. Last night, the S&P 500 edged up 0.16% to 7,734 and the NASDAQ was flat. The big stories in markets are oil surging nearly 2% on Iran war fears (now above US$101/barrel), gold slipping 0.4%, and the Aussie dollar rising 0.3% to US$0.704. All eyes are on Alphabet and Microsoft earnings tonight.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Mild gains last night ahead of big tech earnings.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Essentially flat last night — market in holding pattern before Alphabet and Microsoft results.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil jumped on fears of a US-Iran military flare-up after midterms. Watch your petrol prices.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Slight dip — profit-taking after recent highs. Still elevated overall.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar strengthened a touch. Doesn't change much at this level for your US holdings.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is inflation jumping to 4.3%, well above expectations, which has now tipped market forecasts firmly toward an RBA rate hike next week. The Albanese government is managing expectations on fuel relief, while a major rare earths investment and new digital safety laws also made headlines.

stories.title: Inflation Hits 4.3% — RBA Rate Hike Now Widely Expected Next Tuesday
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's annual inflation rate jumped to 4.3% in the latest quarterly reading, higher than economists expected. CommBank economists are now explicitly forecasting the Reserve Bank will lift the cash rate at its meeting next Tuesday (November 3). AFR reports this is putting simultaneous pressure on Treasurer Chalmers to cut government spending to help ease inflation. For everyday Aussies, a rate rise means higher mortgage repayments — a family with a $600k variable mortgage would pay roughly another $100/month per 0.25% hike.

stories.title: Chalmers Lowers Expectations on Fuel Discount Relief
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers has walked back expectations that the government will deliver meaningful fuel price discounts any time soon, citing the higher-than-expected inflation print as a complicating factor. With oil now above US$101 a barrel due to Middle East tensions, fuel prices at the bowser look set to stay elevated. Not much relief coming for Gold Coast drivers in the near term.

stories.title: Federal Government Commits $180 Million to Rare Earths Mine in Western Victoria
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is investing $180 million in a rare earths mining project in western Victoria. Rare earths are critical inputs for electric vehicles, wind turbines, and defence technology — and Australia is trying to build its own processing capability rather than shipping raw materials to China. This is a signal that the government sees critical minerals as a long-term strategic priority, which is broadly positive context for the sector even if Pilbara Minerals (your PLS.AX) focuses on lithium rather than rare earths.

stories.title: Digital Duty of Care Bill Passes House — AI 'Emotional Intimacy' to Be Banned
stories.why_it_matters: Prime Minister Albanese's Digital Duty of Care Bill has passed the House of Representatives. Critically, the bill would ban AI chatbots from forming 'emotional intimacy' with users — meaning apps like character.ai or companionship chatbots would be prohibited from simulating romantic or deeply personal relationships. Platforms that host harmful content targeting Australians could face significant fines. The bill still needs to pass the Senate. This is part of Australia's broader push to regulate social media and AI, and follows the government's teen social media ban last year.

ai.summary: The headline AI story today is Google's launch of Genie 4, a new world model for real-time interactive simulation — essentially AI that can generate fully interactive, playable environments in real time. Elsewhere, NVIDIA and Meta are expanding their AI collaboration, and the Trump administration rolled back health AI regulation, while debate continues globally about how AI should be governed.

stories.title: Google Launches Genie 4 — AI That Builds Interactive Worlds in Real Time
stories.why_it_matters: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4, described as a 'world model' capable of generating interactive, real-time simulated environments. In plain English: you describe a game world or scenario, and Genie 4 can build a fully playable, interactive version of it on the fly — no traditional game development required. This has huge implications for gaming (relevant to your TTWO holding), education, simulation training, and even robotics. It's a significant step beyond text or image generation into AI that can create entire interactive realities.

stories.title: NVIDIA and Meta Expand Collaboration on Muse AI Models
stories.why_it_matters: NVIDIA and Meta are deepening their partnership around the 'Muse' family of AI models. Muse is Meta's suite of AI tools for generating images, video, and interactive content. NVIDIA's chips power almost all serious AI model training, so this partnership signals continued dominance for both companies in the AI infrastructure space. For your GXAI.AX (AI ETF) holding, this kind of big-tech AI collaboration is exactly the backdrop that should support the sector long-term.

stories.title: Trump Administration Rolls Back Health AI Regulation
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has moved to roll back Obama and Biden-era regulations governing AI used in healthcare settings. In practice, this means fewer mandatory checks on AI tools used for medical diagnosis, treatment recommendations, and hospital administration. Supporters argue it removes red tape and lets innovation move faster; critics worry patients could be harmed by unproven AI making medical decisions. This is part of a broader US trend of deregulating AI ahead of the midterms.

stories.title: Pythia Labs Launches AI-Designed Antibodies for Hard-to-Drug Targets
stories.why_it_matters: A new biotech startup called Pythia Labs has launched with a focus on using AI to design antibody drugs for diseases that have historically been 'undruggable' — meaning existing medicines can't reach or target the relevant proteins. AI is increasingly being used to dramatically speed up the early stages of drug discovery, cutting what used to take years of lab work down to weeks. This is one of the most tangible real-world applications of AI, with potential to unlock treatments for cancers, autoimmune diseases, and rare genetic conditions.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final is done — Roosters beat the Knights 19-18 in a thriller at Accor Stadium. Post-season storylines are now dominating: the Sam Walker contract saga is heating up with Roosters negotiations restarting, Tonga vs Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup is looming, and the AFL trade period is in full swing. Tennis fans are watching Jannik Sinner's new coaching setup ahead of the Australian Open.

stories.title: Roosters Win NRL Grand Final 19-18 Over Knights in Last-Gasp Thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters claimed the 2026 NRL premiership, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 at Accor Stadium in what was a nail-biting one-point finish. Jamayne Isaako is being highlighted as a standout performer heading into international duty with Fiji (the Bati). It's a back-to-back premiership charge for the Roosters and a heartbreaking near-miss for the Knights.

stories.title: Sam Walker Contract Saga: Roosters Restart Negotiations, But Which Club Gets Him?
stories.why_it_matters: Sam Walker's contract future remains the biggest NRL off-season story. The Roosters have restarted negotiations with the star halfback after an extended saga. Braith Anasta says Walker 'doesn't want to go' to one unnamed club, while Bryan Fletcher tips him to sign with a team that won only eight games in 2026 — widely interpreted as pointing toward the Bulldogs or Cowboys. Fox Sports' Ennis called the handling of Walker's situation the 'most disappointing' part of the saga for the Roosters. Resolution is expected soon.

stories.title: Tonga vs Samoa — Rugby League World Cup Too Close to Call
stories.why_it_matters: The Rugby League World Cup is underway, with Tonga and Samoa shaping up as one of the most anticipated Pacific clashes of the tournament. Both sides are loaded with NRL talent and the match is being tipped as too close to call. For Pacific rugby league fans on the Gold Coast, this is must-watch TV.

stories.title: AFL Trade Period Heats Up — Coaching Moves and Draft Prospects in Focus
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL trade period is in full swing, with player movements set to reshape club line-ups heading into 2027. Fox Sports has published predicted 2027 line-ups for every club, highlighting the Roosters' (Cross-code) — sorry, the Sydney Swans' and GWS's — key decisions. Melbourne's Devils are reportedly missing out on two major recruitment targets. The draft is approaching, with a 'generational' ruck prospect being tipped as a potential gamble for two unnamed clubs.

stories.title: Jannik Sinner Appoints Magnus Norman as New Head Coach Ahead of Australian Open
stories.why_it_matters: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner has appointed legendary Swedish coach Magnus Norman — the man who coached Stan Wawrinka to three Grand Slam titles — as his new head coach. A former world No. 4 has already predicted Sinner will win the 2027 Australian Open in January. With the AO just a few months away, this coaching change could be exactly the boost Sinner needs to fend off emerging challengers like Carlos Alcaraz.
